svg.text: Search review, employee, cycle stage, rating, calibration note, or comment
Search cycle stage, self-review, manager review, comment panel, or calibration reason
The left side stays task-led so managers can work the cycle in order rather than hunt for forms
Self-review and manager-review progression stay literal and separate
Queue rows explain why a review is open, pending, or blocked
Calibration markers interrupt finalization when ratings need discussion
Selected appraisal context and decision controls
The active appraisal keeps evidence, panel comments, and final actions in one governed workspace
The manager draft is complete, but one panel comment questions rating consistency against team distribution and requests a hold before final submission.
Next step: compare evidence to the panel note, keep the appraisal on hold if needed, or finalize only when comments and calibration posture are resolved.
Panel comments are visible enough to change the decision path, not buried in history
Finalize and hold states must sit together because reviewers choose between them deliberately
The workspace explains whether missing comments, self-review, or calibration caused the blocker
A good appraisal depends on evidence completeness as much as the final rating choice
Goal completion, check-ins, and competency evidence appear together
Self-review absence remains visible before manager comments begin
Prompting favors strengths, gaps, and next-cycle actions
Comment quality issues can block finalization even when ratings are filled
Calibration posture, hold states, and closure
Cycle governance stays near the active appraisal so reviewers understand why a case can or cannot close
Three reviews are marked for calibration due to team-rating skew
Hold reason is explicit: panel concern, missing self-review, or comment insufficiency
Finalization state appears only after all required signoffs and comments are complete
Closed reviews still preserve the panel chronology for audit and coaching follow-up
Managers and HRBPs can pin cycle stage, self-review, manager-review, calibration, panel comment, and finalize-ready views
This is a PK-QUEUE-01 decision surface first, so the reviewer enters through work that is due.
Self-review, manager-review, hold, and finalize need explicit structure to avoid ambiguous cycle state.
A calibration marker must visibly interrupt closure, not read like a minor note.
Committee or HRBP comments should influence the main decision area, not disappear into a side history.
These are distinct governed outcomes and deserve equal visibility in the control cluster.
Goals, competencies, and comment quality should remain visible beside the rating decision.
The smaller variant focuses on triage and continuation, not full-page drafting.
